grammar.title: Just as expected with 果然
grammar.pattern: (主语) + 果然 + 动词/形容词短语
grammar.explanation: 果然 (guǒrán) means "sure enough, just as expected" — used when something turns out exactly as predicted or guessed. It goes right before the verb or adjective.

grammar.title: Left with no choice but with 只好
grammar.pattern: (主语) + 只好 + 动词短语
grammar.explanation: 只好 (zhǐhǎo) means "to have no choice but to, to have to settle for" — used when the best option left isn't ideal. Compared to 不得不, 只好 focuses more on settling for the only option that remains.

sentences.zh: 他说会下雨，果然下雨了。
sentences.pinyin: Tā shuō huì xiàyǔ, guǒrán xiàyǔ le.
sentences.en: He said it would rain, and sure enough it rained.
This movie was indeed very exciting, as expected.
He passed the exam, just as expected.

sentences.zh: 车坏了，我们只好走路去。
sentences.pinyin: Chē huài le, wǒmen zhǐhǎo zǒulù qù.
sentences.en: The car broke down, so we had to walk there.

sentences.pinyin: Méiyǒu qián, tā zhǐhǎo mài le chē.
sentences.en: Without money, he had no choice but to sell the car.

sentences.zh: 天太晚了，我们只好回家了。
sentences.pinyin: Tiān tài wǎn le, wǒmen zhǐhǎo huíjiā le.
sentences.en: It was too late, so we had to go home.
He still hasn't gotten married, even now.

sentences.zh: 这个问题至今没有解决。
sentences.en: This problem hasn't been solved to this day.

sentences.zh: 他们至今仍然是好朋友。
sentences.pinyin: Tāmen zhìjīn réngrán shì hǎo péngyou.
sentences.en: They're still good friends to this day.
